text.p: Fact file Roberto Baggio, who joined Bologna from AC Milan on Friday: 1967: Born February 18 in Caldogno, northeast Italy. 1982: Makes his professional debut for local side Vicenza in serie C. 1985: Moves to Fiorentina but, after tearing cruciate ligaments in his knee during his last match for Vicenza, misses the better part of two seasons. 1986: Finally makes his serie A debut for Fiorentina against Sampdoria. Fiorentina win 2-0. 1988: Converts to Buddhism. Baggio's hairstyle later earns him the nickname "The Divine Ponytail".

Makes international debut against the Netherlands. Italy win 1-0. 1989: Assumes a more attacking role at Fiorentina, scoring 32 goals in 62 league matches in the 1988-90 seasons. 1990: Moves to Juventus for a then world record $13 million, triggering riots by fans in Florence. 1993: Named European and FIFA world footballer of the year after a spectacular season with Juventus in which he scored 21 goals in 27 league matches and helped them win the UEFA Cup, his first major trophy. 1994: Scores inspired last minute goals against Nigeria and Spain in the United States to keep Italy's World Cup dreams alive. Plays in final despite serious hamstring injury and misses shoot-out penalty which hands the trophy to Brazil. Subsequently dropped by national coach Arrigo Sacchi. 1995: Helps Juventus to their first league title in nine years. Shortly afterwards leaves for arch-rivals Milan for $10.6 million after five seasons in Turin. 1996: Wins second consecutive league title, this time with Milan. Left out of Sacchi's squad for the European championship in England. 1996-97 season: Out of favour with Milan coach Oscar Tabarez who declares: "There's no place for poets in modern soccer." Tabarez replaced by Sacchi mid-season as champions Milan slump to mid-table. Baggio, suffering from sciatica, is still sidelined. June 1997: Misses the four-nation Tournoi de France with a groin strain after finally returning to the national side following a two-year absence. Confirms he will leave Milan. July 18: Signs two-year deal with Bologna for an undisclosed fee.
